newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls, BOLDER in alliance.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls, BOLDER in alliance.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc and BOLDER Technologies Corp, which provides high-power rechargeable batteries, said Wednesday they entered into an agreement to produce and market BOLDER's battery technology.

Specific terms of the agreement were not disclosed, but the companies said BOLDER received a cash payment from Johnson Controls and in return granted Johnson Controls a license to make and sell batteries using BOLDER's patented Thin Metal Film (TMF) technology.

Johnson Controls, which provides automotive systems and building controls, will make TMF products for use in auto/truck starting, hybrid electric vehicles, lawn and garden starting equipment, motorcycle starting and uninterruptible power supply markets. BOLDER said it will receive royalties on all units sold by Johnson Controls.
The companies also said they executed a cross-supply agreement with commitments to supply each other with minimum quantities of TMF battery products for several years.
The first commercial production line of TMF products is in the initial test phase, the companies said.
